correctness.rationale: Seven explicit finite graph models are constructed from stable cyclic pairs. Exhaustive valid-face generation, complete reversed-Hasse acyclicity checks and signed integral Morse boundaries yield the critical counts. Unit integer pivots give rank (d2,d3)=(1,21) at k=6 and (1,9) at k=5, without nonunit factors. One 1/2-cell cancellation makes the 2-skeleton simply connected, so Hurewicz makes 3-cell attaching maps degree vectors, proving the exact wedge classifications. Independent direct mod-two homology checks every reported rank. No inference for k>=7 is made.

value.rationale: Stable two-subset Kneser graphs are a classical vertex-critical family whose ordinary independence homotopy was classified by Braun. Moving to cutoff two is a natural change of graph-complex functor. The complete initial parameter range 0<=k<=6 proves the first qualitative appearance of third homotopy/homology at k=6, not an arbitrary isolated numeric example: the new two S3 summands coexist with 26 S2 summands and no earlier parameter has H3. This integral homotopy boundary is not implied by the ordinary classification and motivates subsequent structural study.
